settings.ggG0APc-eFh_text: Exactly what line items to audit on an IRS Form 1120-S (S-Corp return) to confirm the revenue history is stable, predictable, and free of dangerous customer concentration flags. One customer representing 60% of revenue is not a business — it's a liability. Know before you sign.
settings.ggNm78eME2b_text: Before you structure a deal, you need to know what you're actually buying. These three frameworks separate real cash flow from seller fiction.
settings.ggbCclq3vop_text: The precise mathematical formula to reveal the true, hidden cash flow of any business. Owners legally run personal lifestyle expenses — meals, travel, vehicles, family payroll — through the company to reduce their tax bill. You add those back. Formula: Reported Net Profit + Add-Backs = True Seller's Discretionary Earnings. This single calculation is what separates buyers who overpay from buyers who negotiate.
settings.ggcLkLnXO8J_text: A simple, ruthless strategy to verify that what the seller shows you on the P&L matches what actually hit their bank account. Sellers can manipulate financial statements. They cannot manipulate trailing bank deposits. Run this check before any letter of intent — it guarantees you're not inheriting a fiction dressed up as a business.

settings.gg5DwPtAqDn_text: Protect your financial downside by anchoring a portion of the purchase price to actual, post-sale performance metrics. If the business underperforms what the seller promised, you pay less. This single clause has saved buyers hundreds of thousands of dollars on deals with inflated forward projections.
